# Evidence-Based Prompt Engineering

> A prompt-engineering reference where every technique is graded solid / mixed / folklore, every claim carries a primary source, and model-measured numbers are dated snapshots. By Fernando Aporta Franco (ferinazumaDEV). Version 0.1.0 · 2026-09-04 · CC BY-SA 4.0 prose, CC BY 4.0 data and templates, MIT code.

## Core
- [Evidence ledger (techniques)](data/techniques.yml): graded, sourced table of techniques — the machine-readable heart of the repo.
- [Claims and maturity](CLAIMS.md): the grading vocabulary, the alias solid == established, and the register of claims that have no ledger row yet.
- [Folklore, debunked](FOLKLORE.md): widely repeated prompt "tricks" with no reproducible evidence.
- [Security](docs/05-security.md): prompt injection, the lethal trifecta, and architecture-level defenses.
- [Technique selector](docs/08-technique-selector.md): which technique for which problem.

## Reference
- [Archived releases (Zenodo)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22307826): every tagged release archived with a DOI; this concept DOI always resolves to the latest one. Cite this rather than the repository URL.
- [README](README.md): what this is, how grading works, scope.
- [Sources](SOURCES.md): primary papers with arXiv/DOI.
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md): versioned history — every grade change and the evidence that moved it.
- [About (machine-readable)](about.jsonld): schema.org JSON-LD — source of truth for name, author, version, DOI, dateModified, maturity.
- [How to cite](CITATION.cff): Aporta Franco, Fernando. Evidence-Based Prompt Engineering, v0.1.0 (2026-09-04). DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22307826.
